summary.text: A continuous variable has possible values between any two of its values, so one that ranges over the real numbers can take any value in that range.
Methods of calculus are often used for problems with continuous variables, such as continuous optimization.
In statistics, the probability distributions of continuous variables can be expressed with probability density functions.

facts.label: Defining test
facts.value: Possible values exist between any two values

facts.label: Mixed case
facts.value: A variable can be continuous in some ranges, discrete in others

facts.label: Calculus
facts.value: Often used in problems with continuous variables

items.prompt: An idealised thermometer can show any value from 20 to 30 degrees. Why is this reading a continuous variable?

options.label: Between any two possible readings there is another possible reading
It is read from an instrument rather than counted
Its readings are written out with decimal points
It changes as time goes by

items.explain: A continuous variable is one with possible values between any two values, as with a variable over a range of the real numbers.

items.prompt: A model lets time flow smoothly, with every instant allowed. What kind of equation describes how a variable evolves?
items.explain: In continuous-time dynamics, time is treated as continuous and the evolution is described by a differential equation.

items.prompt: A statistician describes the distribution of a continuous variable. Which tool is the usual one?
items.explain: The probability distributions of continuous variables can be expressed with probability density functions. Mass functions are for discrete variables.

items.prompt: Someone says a variable allowed only the values 1, 2 and 3 is continuous because those are real numbers. Where is the mistake?

options.label: Real numbers can never form a continuous variable
The variable would have to be able to take 0 as well
The variable would have to be written with decimals
There are no possible values between 1 and 2, so it is not continuous

items.explain: A continuous variable needs possible values between any two values. Here there is a gap around each value, so it is discrete.

items.prompt: Which job is calculus better suited to: tuning a dial that turns smoothly, or picking a whole number of trucks to rent?

options.label: Picking the whole number of trucks
Neither, calculus only deals with time

items.explain: Methods of calculus are often used with continuous variables, as in continuous optimization, and do not readily suit discrete variables such as integer programming.

items.prompt: A study of psychological disorder risk uses a yes/no symptom measure and also a smooth cognitive score. What is this an example of?
items.explain: A study with one binary measure and one continuous measure is an example of a mixed model.
